C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE.Summary: Give mt_search_spawn a real files mode, closing the Wave-3 bundle-3 criterion «в режиме имён инструментированная фикстура подтверждает отсутствие чтения тел файлов» (in name-search mode an instrumented fixture confirms file bodies are not read): mode "files" stops spawning a content search with the empty pattern — the backend enumerates file paths only (the embedded walker leg without a single body open; an `rg --files` listing transport for the shell-out leg), the dead `inclusions` option is wired as a symmetric whitelist glob filter on both legs, a named delivered-paths cap (FILES_RESULT_CAP = 30, the number of the removed ">30 files" promise) bounds the per-keystroke traversal and honestly marks the truncated set partial through the #303 flag, and the paths stream as path-only hits through the existing match-kind envelope so the #320 grouped-envelope contract and quickOpen's string ids keep working unchanged. No renderer production file changes.
C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the green-search3 worktree (branch spec/quickopen-files-mode, base 486275c7, which already carries C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT (#320) and C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD (#324); the scout's pre-#320 line anchors have shifted and are re-verified here); source findings are WAVE3-SCOUT-SEARCH (2026-11-22) key QO-READS-CONTENTS (6) plus the quick-open ">30 files" residue of key SEARCH-LIMIT-UNREACHABLE (5). Mode ignored: src/renderer/src/node/fileSearcher.js sends "this._spawn('files', directories, '', options)" (:8-10), but the backend discards the discriminator — "let _ = mode;" (src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs:650, inside mt_search_spawn) — and runs the content session with the pattern quickOpen passed, which is the empty string (quickOpen.js ".search([rootPath], '', …)" :146). The empty pattern matches every line of every file: the embedded walker opens each body ("std::fs::File::open(file_path)" :556, "reader.lines()" :561, "matcher.find_iter(&line)" :580) and the rg transport builds a content command even for files mode ("cmd.arg("--").arg(pattern).arg(root)" :815 behind START_BLOCK_BUILD_RIPGREP_COMMAND :781-817, where an empty --fixed-strings pattern matches every line) — every quick-open keystroke fully reads the bodies of the whole root and streams meaningless per-line hits. Inclusions dead: SearchOptions carries "pub inclusions: Option<Vec<String>>" (:98) under a struct-level "#[allow(dead_code)]" whose own comment says "inclusions globs are part of the contract but not yet wired into run_search" (:81-84), although the renderer half has always been live — quickOpen passes "inclusions: this._getInclusions(query)" (:171) and the searcher serializes 'inclusions' across IPC (ripgrepSearcher.js :119-131) — so the name filter the palette computes never reaches either engine. No honest area limit: quickOpen's self-limit "if (!canceled && numPathsFound > 30) { canceled = true … }" waited for a searchedPaths event the wire never delivers; #324 removed it as dead code and its replacement comment defers exactly this change — "The files-mode cost and limit design stays with C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE." (quickOpen.js :165-168) — so today a quick-open keystroke pays an unbounded full traversal with no cap and no partial honesty. The scout's amplification of key 6 (didMatch receiving grouped envelope objects where quickOpen expected strings) is already closed on this baseline by #320's consumer-side normalization (quickOpen.js :147-164), which is verified against today's content-spawn envelope precisely so it keeps working when this change lands.
C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE.Relationship: Direct successor of C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION (merged as #289), C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY (merged as #303, status applied) and C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT (merged as #320, authored in the green-search1 worktree, now archived); lands on top of C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD (#324, authored in the green-search2 worktree, present on this baseline with its graph and verification deltas). #289's SearchSessionCoordinator keeps sole ownership of the session-wide seq and the single terminal — the files-mode session streams match batches through the same coordinator and finalizes only through run_session's discipline, so terminal ownership is untouched by construction. #303's honest voice is reused, not weakened: the additive optional SearchEvent.partial flag (absent-field serialization) carries the files-mode cap and suppression honesty exactly as it carries size limits and exclusion masks today, and the #303 error voice (failures only, stable messages) governs the files-mode rg transport identically. #320's contract is preserved verbatim: the shim's mt::search-event translation stays the single funnel and is not edited; path-only hits group per path into the same "filePath" plus "matches" envelope, quickOpen's didMatch normalization (:147-164) keeps producing string ids, and the no-shim-mode-map pin ("the shim gains no per-searchId mode map") holds because no mode state leaves the backend. #324's cap precedent is reused as the honesty model — SEARCH_RESULT_CAP = 100 (store/search.js :119) caps delivered matches and marks the set partial; this change applies the same delivered-result-unit honesty on the backend side where the cost lives — and #324's own deferral comment names this change as the owner of the files-mode cost and limit design. Sibling bundles from the same scout stay NonGoals and separable: C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY (case divergence, gitignore-outside, UTF-8 truncation, tree cost — the W3d separate bundle). Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: mode "files" runs a real name-mode session: mt_search_spawn branches on the discriminator instead of discarding it, and the files-mode session walks every validated root through the same coordinator with the same engine selection (App Store in-process walker, missing-rg fallback, rg shell-out otherwise), per-root traversal order, batch size, registry lifecycle and 120 ms warm-up as content mode. The embedded walker leg enumerates file paths without opening a single file body — no File::open, no line reading, no content matcher; the rg leg runs the `rg --files` listing transport instead of the pattern search. The pattern and the content-matcher options (isRegexp/isCaseSensitive/isWholeWord) are ignored in files mode — an invalid content pattern can never fail a files search.

The dead inclusions option is wired as a whitelist name filter applied symmetrically by both legs, under one documented glob semantics defined once (the compile_exclusion_masks canon: matching against the path relative to the root, a bare glob without "/" matches the basename at any depth, "*" does not cross path separators, case-sensitive): the walker applies valid inclusion globs through ignore's whitelist overrides, the rg transport passes each valid glob verbatim as a `--glob=` argument; an invalid inclusion glob is explicitly ignored by both legs (never passed to rg, never used by the walker) and only forces the session's honest partial flag. Exclusions keep their #303 semantics unchanged in files mode (walker pruning plus `--glob=!` arguments, valid masks force partial). Valid inclusions never force partial by themselves — they define the requested domain the way the pattern does in content mode, and quickOpen passes them on every query; absent or empty inclusions mean no name filter (all traversed files, subject to cap, ignore rules and exclusions).

An honest area cap replaces the dead ">30 files" promise: a named constant FILES_RESULT_CAP = 30 bounds the delivered path hits per files-mode session (the unit the consumer collects, #324's delivered-result precedent). When the cap fires, both legs stop the traversal promptly, the delivered set is truncated to the cap exactly, and the session's single terminal completes with partial = true through the existing #303 additive flag — a cap is not a failure and not a cancellation: the error voice stays empty and no capped set is ever presented as complete. The renderer stays untouched: the palette gains no partial notice and no new UI; the honest flag rides the wire for any future consumer.

Files-mode results ride the existing wire contract as path-only hits: one SearchHit per delivered file path through the existing match event kind, carrying the path, line 0, column 0, an empty snippet, truncated false and wire-absent matchStart/matchEnd (the struct's established skip_serializing_if style). No new event kind, channel or envelope field; the grouped renderer envelope, the shim translation and quickOpen's string ids keep working unchanged; project-search consumers are unaffected because they never send mode "files".

An instrumented fixture proves bodies are not read, deterministically and without flaky filesystem metadata: on one temp-dir fixture, an unreadable decoy (Unix permission-gated, name matching the inclusion globs) is delivered by files mode — a body read would fail its open and silently skip it, exactly as today's content spawn does — while a body-bait decoy (name missing the inclusion globs, body containing the query text) is never delivered, and every delivered hit is pinned path-only. Both supported engines are pinned individually on the same fixture: the walker leg always, the rg leg under the existing availability guard.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep the existing command names (mt_search_spawn, mt_search_cancel), the mt::search-event channel, searchId, the SearchEvent kinds (match/complete/cancelled/error) and envelope (hits/error/partial/seq), DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, M-010 root validation before registry insert, the registry lifecycle (insert on spawn, remove after the worker finishes), the 120 ms listen warm-up, engine selection (app-store in-process, missing-rg fallback with BLOCK_RIPGREP_FALLBACK) and ordinary root traversal order. No new terminal kind, channel or envelope field. Content mode is untouched: run_session, both content engine legs, build_matcher, compile_exclusion_masks and the #303 partial formula keep their current behavior byte-for-byte, and every existing backend suite keeps its assertions and budgets.

The files-mode session mirrors run_session's structure with the same discipline: a files-mode session function owning the per-root loop, the honest partial computation and the single terminal through the coordinator; a walker path leg (same WalkBuilder filter setup — standard filters, hidden, ignore rules, require_git(false), symlink following, exclusion overrides — with the body scan removed); an `rg --files` transport inheriting #303's honesty machinery (bounded BLOCK-log-only stderr capture, exit-status check — codes 0 and 1 complete normally, any other exit or a signal is the single "rg exited with code N" error class whose message carries the code only — and the cancel watcher that kills and reaps a silent child); and an rg-program injection seam mirroring run_session_with_program so spawn-failure and exit-2 tests stay deterministic under parallel cargo test. The walker leg keeps its between-entry cancel checks; terminals are owned solely by the coordinator.

Inclusion semantics are documented exactly once beside the exclusion canon they extend: valid globs are applied symmetrically (walker whitelist overrides built on the root; rg `--glob=` arguments verbatim); an invalid glob (empty/whitespace-only, NUL byte, or a glob the engine rejects) is explicitly ignored by both legs and increments the ignored count so the terminal forces the honest partial flag. The files-mode complete-terminal partial formula carries the #303 triggers over unchanged (an active size limit, at least one valid exclusion mask, any ignored invalid glob — exclusion or inclusion) and grows exactly one new trigger: the files cap having fired.

Cap specifics: one named documented constant FILES_RESULT_CAP = 30 — the number of the removed quick-open promise — counted on delivered path hits per session, the set truncated to the constant exactly even when the crossing batch overshot, both legs stopping promptly on the cap, the single terminal completing with partial = true, no capped set presented as complete, the error state untouched, and the cap never emitting a second terminal or a cancellation. The plan may adjust the number only with documented rationale (the #324 precedent: honesty is the contract, not the count).

The path-only hit form is pinned: a files-mode hit never carries a non-empty snippet, a non-zero line or column, or matchStart/matchEnd values; the wire form keeps the struct's established serialization (snippet serialized as the empty string, bounds wire-absent). The shim, ripgrepSearcher, fileSearcher, quickOpen, store/search.js, the palette and the typed facade gain no production edits — renderer pins for files mode are additive test-only.

No new user-facing strings: the palette renders no files-mode partial notice and no new copy; the honest marker exists on the wire only. If the plan nonetheless introduces a user-visible string, it lands under the established namespace in all ten locale files (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW) following the C-62 all-locales pattern, gated by the locale-keys test.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY work (the W3d separate bundle): no smart-case or gitignore-outside alignment, no UTF-8 byte-slice truncation fix, no tree-emit batching, no engine unification, no rg sidecar bundling. Known content-engine divergences stay recorded; this change only pins files-mode behavior per leg on one fixture and keeps both files-mode legs semantically identical.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first backend proof that bodies are not read: on the instrumented fixture (matching-name files, an unreadable permission decoy — #[cfg(unix)], name matching the inclusions — and a body-bait decoy whose name misses the inclusions while its body contains the query text), a files-mode walker session delivers the unreadable decoy, never delivers the body-bait, and every delivered hit is path-only (empty snippet, line 0, column 0, wire-absent bounds). Today the mode is discarded and the content spawn with the empty pattern cannot deliver the unreadable decoy (its open fails and the entry is skipped), does deliver the body-bait, and streams body-derived snippets — so every assertion of this test is red before the fix. The fixture also pins a nested-directory file matching a bare inclusion glob (basename at any depth).

Inclusion tests pin both legs symmetrically on one fixture: valid inclusion globs whitelist exactly the matching names in the walker leg and, availability-guarded, in the rg --files leg; an invalid inclusion glob is explicitly ignored by both legs and forces the honest partial flag on the single terminal; exclusions remain excluded in files mode alongside inclusions (a masked file absent, an unmasked sibling present, both legs); valid inclusions alone complete with partial = false; absent or empty inclusions deliver all traversed files subject to the cap.

Failing-first cap test: a fixture with more matching files than FILES_RESULT_CAP ends with exactly the cap delivered across the session's match events, the single complete terminal carrying partial = true, zero post-terminal events (full-trace collection), and the same truncation semantics under the rg leg (availability-guarded); a fixture below the cap completes with the honest non-partial terminal. Today no cap exists on any path, so the truncation assertions are red before the fix.

Files-mode rg transport honesty: an injected rg program (an impossible path, and an exit-2 script via the existing write_exec_script seam) yields exactly one error terminal with the stable exit-code class, remaining roots not started and the partial marker when hits were already streamed; codes 0 and 1 complete normally; a pre-cancelled files-mode session yields exactly one cancelled terminal with no match events and the walker's between-entry cancel discipline holds (mid-walk cancel drains the pending batch, then cancels).

Renderer compatibility pins (additive, test-only): the shim translation maps a path-only hit into the grouped envelope with the zero-pair range row and no fabricated span (extending the shim-range-array-form family), and quickOpen resolves string ids from that files-mode grouped envelope with executeSubcommand sending the string pathname to mt::open-file-by-window-id (extending the #320 shim-shaped-feed pins). Every existing quickOpen, fileSearcher, store, shim C-52 and searchResultItem suite stays green unchanged.

Graph and verification describe the final state: M-004's module map grows the files-mode session, walker path leg, rg --files transport, inclusion validation and FILES_RESULT_CAP entries with a SummaryDelta; M-011's SummaryDelta documents the unchanged consumer compatibility (grouped envelope, string ids, no shim mode map); V-M-004 and V-M-011 entries carry the new evidence; all pre-existing suites — the #289 session-trace family, the #303 honest-state family, the #320 range/keyboard/quickOpen-string-id family, the #324 store-cap and lifecycle family, the shim C-52 boot-order pins and the e2e search-bar spec — pass without weakened assertions or budgets. M-013 stays a read-only adjacency (its stub records name the facade and commands; no M-013 file is edited).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Named new tests pin the behaviors: files-mode-walker-lists-paths-without-reading-bodies (unreadable permission decoy delivered via the name-only decision, body-bait never delivered, path-only hit shape, nested bare-glob match), files-mode-inclusions-filter-both-legs (whitelist symmetry, invalid glob ignored and partial-forcing, exclusions still excluded, valid inclusions alone not partial), files-mode-cap-truncates-and-marks-partial (exact truncation, single complete terminal with partial = true, no post-terminal events), files-mode-rg-transport-honesty (injected spawn failure and exit-2 error class, codes 0/1 normal, pre-cancelled single cancelled terminal), files-mode-rg-parity-with-walker-on-one-fixture (availability-guarded, identical expected path sets), plus the additive renderer pins shim-path-only-hit-mapping and quickopen-files-mode-string-ids. Existing #289 session-trace, #303 honest-state, #320 contract, #324 lifecycle-cap, quickOpen, fileSearcher and C-52 receipts are preserved as pre-change evidence, not relabeled.

App Store and missing-rg fallback paths are exercised through the in-process walker suites; native rg behavior stays guarded by the existing availability checks with the canon skip marker. The unreadable-decoy proof is #[cfg(unix)] and its gating is documented in the change record — Windows coverage rides the shape, inclusion and cap pins, which run everywhere. Unavailable platform or owner acceptance evidence remains explicitly open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The cap preserves the removed promise's number (30 delivered path hits per session) as the named FILES_RESULT_CAP; the plan may adjust the number with documented rationale — the acceptance criterion is the honest truncation and partial marker, not the specific count (the #324 precedent, where SEARCH_RESULT_CAP = 100 preserved that promise's number).

The cap is backend-side by decision: the cost defect is the backend traversal itself (a full root walk per keystroke), so the honest fix bounds the walk instead of discarding results after the fact; a renderer-side quickOpen cap was considered and rejected because it would leave the unbounded traversal alive and force new palette UI for the partial notice, while the #303 wire flag already carries the honesty. Files mode is reachable only from quickOpen (fileSearcher is its only sender), so the backend cap does not affect project search.

Inclusion globs pass verbatim with gitignore-style semantics — case-sensitive by default, bare globs matching basenames at any depth — identical on both legs (the ignore overrides engine and rg --glob defaults agree); quickOpen's tab matching stays case-insensitive renderer-side, so a mixed-case query filters disk results case-sensitively exactly as v1's rg-based behavior did. This is recorded v1 parity, not a new divergence.

The body-read proof uses filesystem-permission decoys rather than a read counter: an atime check is unreliable under relatime/noatime mounts and test parallelism; a FIFO decoy is useless because FileType::is_file() is false for one, so both legs skip it before any open; a production CountingWalker seam would prove only that the seam is not called, not that the real path does not read — the zone's injection precedents (run_session_with_program, the rg-program scripts) inject real programs, not counters. The permission decoy is the direct behavioral proof: if the files-mode leg ever grows a body read, the decoy vanishes from the result set and the test goes red.

The `rg --files` listing does not apply --max-filesize (a content-search-time filter), while the walker's metadata skip does not read bodies either; the plan documents the per-transport size handling and keeps the parity fixture below any configured limit — quickOpen never sends maxFileSize, and any files-mode size divergence note belongs to C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY, not here.

Siblings #320 and #324 are present on the delivery baseline before this change lands; the plan re-verifies the shared anchors (the quickOpen didMatch consumer, the shim translation family, the store cap) and reruns their suites. Approval of this specification does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.
